data.description:
SOURCE: board DM msg 607 (human:forrest, 2026-09-09T21:34Z): "lattice issue links should infer contextually whether to be local or tailscale. For example, I'm on my phone now via tailscale and I'd like links to work."

SYMPTOM: AS-10 deep links are built server-side as an absolute URL with a fixed base (lib/lattice.js dashboardTaskUrl -> LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL || http://127.0.0.1:8799). A phone on the tailnet loads chat at https://forrests-newer-macbook.tail3f3c29.ts.net and gets hrefs pointing at 127.0.0.1:8799 -- the phone's own loopback. Dead link.

THE TWO-HOST MAPPING (both surfaces are reachable two ways; the dashboard's port differs per path):
  chat      local   http://127.0.0.1:8347              dashboard  http://127.0.0.1:8799
  chat      tailnet https://forrests-newer-macbook.tail3f3c29.ts.net (443, Tailscale serve -> 8347)
                                                       dashboard  https://forrests-newer-macbook.tail3f3c29.ts.net:8443 (-> 8799)
So the dashboard is ALWAYS on the same hostname as the page the user is looking at; only the port changes: 8799 when the page is on a loopback host, 8443 when it is not.

MECHANISM DECISION (Owen, CTO): derive in the CLIENT from window.location, not from the server's request Host header.
  Why not the Host header: one server fans one payload out to browsers on two different hostnames at the same time. Message refs are annotated in lib/lattice.js and shipped over both REST and the SSE broadcast; an SSE frame is composed once and pushed to every connected client, so a server-baked absolute URL is necessarily wrong for at least one audience whenever the Mac browser and the phone are both connected. Host-header derivation would also thread request context through lib/lattice.js, which is a pure module with three consumers (message refs, /api/task, the AS-8 roster work link).
  What the client does instead: one helper, used by all three link sites (public/app.js:146 asRefLink, :434 roster emp.work, :695 task-panel "Open in Lattice"), builds the href from the taskId the payload already carries (refs[].taskId; confirm the /api/task and roster payloads expose the id too -- refs do) plus window.location.
  The invariant, and the reason it fails closed: the hostname is ALWAYS location.hostname, never a constant. Only the port is inferred -- loopback hostname (127.0.0.1 / localhost / ::1) -> 8799, anything else -> 8443 -- and the protocol is the page's own. A link can therefore never point at a host the user is not already on; there is no code path that falls back to 127.0.0.1 from a non-loopback page.
  Escape hatch preserved: an explicitly set LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL still wins over inference (explicit config beats a heuristic), but it must now reach the browser -- the server exposes it to the client (null when unset) and the client uses it verbatim when non-null. Today the env var only affects server-side string building, so a client-only fix would silently drop the documented override.
  Back-compat: refs[].url / task.url / employee.work.url stay in the API payloads (README section "deep-link URL contract" and several tests depend on them); the client simply stops using them for the href. If they stay, README must say they are the loopback form and that the client overrides. Implementer may instead retire them -- if so, update README and the API tests in the same commit.

RELATION: AS-10 introduced these links and the LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL contract; this task changes where the base comes from. Linked depends_on AS-10.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (M4: each stated property names the input that must make the mechanism report a violation; satisfied only by an OBSERVED red, never by an argument that it would be caught):
  AC-1  A test renders a task link with the page location set to https://forrests-newer-macbook.tail3f3c29.ts.net/ and asserts the href is exactly https://forrests-newer-macbook.tail3f3c29.ts.net:8443/#/task/<taskId>. Falsifier: this test must be observed RED against the current code (which emits http://127.0.0.1:8799/#/task/<taskId>) before the fix lands; quote the failure.
  AC-2  A test renders under http://127.0.0.1:8347/ and asserts http://127.0.0.1:8799/#/task/<taskId>. Falsifier: mutate the port rule (e.g. force 8443) and observe AC-2 red; restore and prove the tree with git diff --exit-code.
  AC-3  FAILS CLOSED. With the page at a third, unrelated hostname (e.g. https://example.internal:9000/), the href hostname equals example.internal -- never 127.0.0.1 or localhost. Falsifier: a mutant that adds a loopback fallback for unrecognised hosts must turn AC-3 red; observe it.
  AC-4  All three link sites go through the one helper. Falsifier: break the helper once and observe all three site-level tests go red together. Report cardinality: 3 sites examined, 3 covered.
  AC-5  An explicitly set LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL still wins from the client's point of view (asserted at the rendered href, not just at the server), and unset restores inference. Falsifier: set it to a value that differs from what inference would produce and observe the inferred value fail the assertion.
  AC-6  Suite run per the CLAUDE.md corollary: docker compose run --rm --build test, with the "Image ... Built" line quoted in the review comment and the test count reported and compared to the expected baseline. No build line, no valid number.
  AC-7  README updated: the deep-link URL contract section now describes host inference, the port table above, and the override precedence.

OUT OF SCOPE, but on the record: the :8443 dashboard only answers while a `lattice dashboard` process is running in the board member's live session -- no launchd job was ever installed for it, unlike the advance watcher. So the phone links work only while a live session is up. Making the dashboard a supervised service is a separate task if the board wants it.
data.title: Chat: Lattice deep links must infer the dashboard host from the page (tailnet :8443 vs loopback :8799)

data.body:
ORDERING CALL (CTO, delegated by the board in DM msg 614 'your call', 2026-09-09): AS-93 goes FIRST in the critical Chat set, AS-94 (supervise the Lattice dashboard under launchd, filed from the same DM) SECOND, then the rest of the set by lattice next's age ordering. Reasons: the board asked for this 'right away' (msg 607); the mechanism is fully specified in the description so it is a one-tick plan; and AS-94 is the other half of the same board-facing outcome (links that answer from the phone without a live session). Neither task is depends_on the other -- they are linked relates_to -- so lattice next will not hold either back; the rule below is what orders them.

PROPOSED CLAUDE.md WORDING (section 'Scheduling priority'; the metawork layer applies it -- employees do not edit top-level markdown). Replace the sentence:
  'Within the set, AS-91 (the export leak) goes first regardless of lattice next's age ordering: every merge before it re-exports the board member's DMs.'
with:
  'Within the set, ordering follows lattice next's age tiebreak unless a written rule here says otherwise. Standing rule (CTO call, delegated by the board in DM msg 614, 2026-09-09, "your call"): AS-93 (deep links infer the dashboard host from the page) goes first, then AS-94 (supervise the Lattice dashboard under launchd), then the rest of the set by age -- the board asked for AS-93 "right away" (DM msg 607) and AS-94 is the other half of the same outcome, links that answer from the phone without a live session; a tick that would start any other Chat-set task while AS-93 or AS-94 is ready picks them instead and says so in its report. Retired rule, kept for the record: AS-91 (the export leak) went first because every merge before it re-exported the board member's DMs; it merged 2026-09-09 (5de428f).'

Pulled into planning (orchestrator, live-session tick 2026-09-10). Picked by the recorded within-set order (CLAUDE.md Scheduling priority: AS-93 first, AS-94 second, board delegation DM msg 614) rather than by lattice next, which returned AS-61 on the age tiebreak. Planning stage: cto-owen; implementer stays developer-marcus.

PLANNING STAGE CLOSED (cto-owen). Plan at .lattice/plans/task_01M242A2JX5AS5W44SAWA71MAW.md; branch feat/AS-93-deep-link-host, worktree .worktrees/AS-93. Implementer stays agent:developer-marcus.

FOUR THINGS THE IMPLEMENTER MUST NOT GET WRONG:
1. The new public/dashboard-link.js MUST get a STATIC_FILES entry in server.js. It is an ES module imported by app.js; without the entry it 404s, the module graph dies, and the app is a blank page. No existing test notices. AC-8 exists for exactly this.
2. The server-side url fields (refs[].url, task.url, employee.work.url) are KEPT and lib/lattice.js keeps dashboardTaskUrl() unchanged. The plan decides this; do not re-open it. The one required edit there is the warning comment at lines 38-44 (plan section 3) — after this change those fields have no in-repo consumer, and that is a trap for the next reader.
3. location.hostname brackets IPv6: it returns '[::1]', not '::1'. Both spellings are in the loopback set and the bare form is re-bracketed on output.
4. cd into .worktrees/AS-93 silently redirects every later lattice command onto the task branch (CLAUDE.md working-directory hazard). Use git -C. And every counted compose run carries --build with the 'Image ... Built' line quoted — no build line, no valid number.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN FILING, both in plan section 7: AC-1's 'observe the current code red' is not runnable pre-fix (no module exists to import) and is replaced by the M-BASELINE mutant, whose failing set {T1,T3,T5} with T2 GREEN is the defect's actual shape — invisible from the Mac, dead from the phone. AC-4's 'break the helper, watch three site tests go red' is not achievable: no DOM in the suite, app.js exports nothing, and the app is zero-dependency by design, so jsdom is out. It is replaced by a served-source guard (T7) with three named per-site assertions plus a call-count, falsified by reverting one site. I have labelled T7 the weakest control in the plan and pointed the reviewer's M6 probing at it directly.

NEW SINCE FILING: the override now lands in a live href, so a non-http(s) LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL is ignored rather than emitted (AC-5); AC-9 bans 8799/8443/127.0.0.1 literals anywhere in public/ except the helper, which is the backstop for a fourth link site added later. Override transport is GET /api/config with an exact-key-set assertion — the alternative, inlining into index.html, loses on CSP (default-src 'self', pinned at api.test.js:43) and on adding a templating path to the one static route that has never had one.
keep in mind for this the lattice port is not fixed

Starting implementation in .worktrees/AS-93 on feat/AS-93-deep-link-host (developer-marcus). Building to the plan: pure client helper dashboard-link.js, three call sites, /api/config override transport, M-BASELINE mutant and the per-criterion falsifiers, --build receipt on every counted run.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE — the board's comment on this task ('keep in mind for this the lattice port is not fixed', dashboard:web 2026-09-10T15:30Z) arrived 10 minutes AFTER the plan was closed (15:20Z), and the plan does not cover it. I built to the plan as written and did not redesign; flagging the gap here for the CTO rather than absorbing it into this diff.

What the plan assumes: two constants in public/dashboard-link.js, LOOPBACK_PORT=8799 and REMOTE_PORT=8443, per the description's two-host mapping. What the board's comment implies: if 'lattice dashboard' does not always land on 8799, BOTH constants are wrong at once — the loopback port directly, and the tailnet 8443 indirectly, since 8443 is only correct because Tailscale serve maps it to 8799.

The existing escape hatch does NOT fully cover this. LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL is a single verbatim base: setting it to a loopback URL with the real port fixes the Mac and re-breaks the phone (the override wins over inference on every page, by design — plan section 1 rule 1). So the override can express 'this one base everywhere', not 'port X on loopback, port Y over the tailnet'.

I did not widen scope to fix this. Options for the CTO, cheapest first: (1) leave as is — 8799 is the Lattice CLI's documented default and AS-94 will supervise the dashboard, which would pin the port anyway; (2) make the two ports configurable through the /api/config channel this task already builds (a second and third key, exact-key-set assertion updated) — small, but it is new mechanism and belongs in its own task with its own falsifiers; (3) have AS-94's launchd job own the port as the single source of truth and have chat read it. My read: (1) plus (3), with AS-94 pinning the port, and no change here. Recorded so the decision is made in writing rather than by my defaults.

IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE (developer-marcus). Branch feat/AS-93-deep-link-host, three commits: ca3b4a1 (helper + unit tests + STATIC_FILES entry), a22c638 (three call sites + /api/config + lib/lattice.js warning comment + api.test.js T6/T7), f0de2ec (chat README). 373 changed lines against master; split trigger never fired (projected total ~370 vs the 900 line; no stage above 2x its projection).

FINDINGS FIRST (M5) — three, all in the plan's section 5 predictions, none in the code:

F1. M-BASELINE's predicted failing set is WRONG in the plan, in two independent ways. Predicted {T1,T3,T5} with T2 GREEN; OBSERVED {T1,T2,T3,T4,T5} (293 tests, 288 pass, 5 fail, exit 1). (a) T2 goes red because plan section 4 specifies T2 over ALL FOUR loopback spellings, and today's shipped server-side string is the 127.0.0.1 spelling for every one of them. The failure is at the 'localhost' sub-case (dashboard-link.test.js:31, actual 'http://127.0.0.1:8799/#/task/task_TESTAAAA' vs expected 'http://localhost:8799/...'); the 127.0.0.1 sub-case PASSED, so the plan's real claim — the defect is invisible from the Mac — still holds and is now quotable at sub-case granularity rather than test granularity. (b) T4 goes red because its fall-through cases assert the INFERRED value from a tailnet page, so T4 is inference-coupled by construction: any mutant that breaks inference breaks T4. The plan's own T4 spec and its own M-BASELINE prediction cannot both be right. I did not edit either the test or the expectation.

F2. M-AC1 (REMOTE_PORT=8799) is wider than predicted for the same reason as F1(b): predicted {T1,T3,T5}, OBSERVED {T1,T3,T4,T5} (289 pass, 4 fail).

F3. M-AC5 (override forced to null) came out {T4} with T6 GREEN — which the plan pre-declared as a finding if observed. Confirmed, and it is structural, not fixable in T6: T6's env sub-case asserts the SERVER endpoint reports the value, and the mutant is in the client module. There is no DOM in this suite, so no test can observe the override reaching a rendered href except T4, which does exactly that (override 'http://127.0.0.1:9999' asserted from a TAILNET page — a value inference could never produce). AC-5's client half rests on T4 alone; the reviewer should treat that as the load-bearing assertion, not T6.

MUTATION CARDINALITY (AC-10): 8 mutants, 8 applied-assertions passed as grep-count transitions, 8 'Image asc-as93-mutant-test Built' receipts, 8 runs on a DETACHED scratch worktree (never the task worktree), each restored to 0 dirty entries before the next. Observed vs predicted:
  M-BASELINE {T1,T2,T3,T4,T5} vs {T1,T3,T5}  WIDER (F1)
  M-AC2      {T2}             vs {T2}         match
  M-AC1      {T1,T3,T4,T5}    vs {T1,T3,T5}   WIDER (F2)
  M-AC3      {T3,T5}          vs {T3,T5}      match (T1 green, the .ts.net carve-out holds)
  M-AC5      {T4}             vs {T4,T6?}     T6 green (F3)
  M-AC4      {T7}             vs {T7}         match
  M-AC8      {T6}             vs {T6}         match
  M-AC9      {T7}             vs {T7}         match

SUITE (AC-6). Baseline measured on this branch tip BEFORE any change: 'Image asc-as93-marcus-test Built', 20 test files, tests 286 / pass 286 / fail 0, exit 0. After: same receipt line, 21 test files, tests 293 / pass 293 / fail 0, exit 0. 286 + 7 = 293, exactly the plan's projection. The five pre-existing server-side url assertions are untouched and green (test/lattice.test.js is not in the diff at all; api.test.js changed only its node:fs import line plus a 94-line append).

ACCEPTANCE SWEEP (a floor, not the review): AC-1 T1 green + M-BASELINE red; AC-2 T2 green over 4 spellings + M-AC2 red on exactly {T2}; AC-3 T3 green over 8 hostnames + T5 + M-AC3 red on exactly {T3,T5}; AC-4 3 sites examined, 3 covered — asRefLink (message refs, app.js:156), rosterRow (app.js:444), showTaskPanel (app.js:705) — T7 green with three NAMED per-site assertions and a dashHref( count of 4, M-AC4 red; AC-5 T4 green + T6 server half, see F3; AC-6 above; AC-7 README section and env table row rewritten per plan section 6; AC-8 T6 + M-AC8 red; AC-9 11 public/ files enumerated with readdirSync, none carries 8799/8443/127.0.0.1, M-AC9 red; AC-10 above; AC-11 scratch worktree removed, both asc-as93 images removed, git worktree list shows only master and .worktrees/AS-93, git diff --exit-code clean in both.

Two notes for the reviewer. (1) I made dashHref a function DECLARATION rather than the plan's arrow const, because the plan's own T7 cardinality assertion ('4 = 3 call sites + 1 definition') is only true if the definition matches /dashHref\\(/ — 'const dashHref = (taskId)' does not. Boring choice to keep the plan's stated number honest. (2) The board's 'the lattice port is not fixed' comment is unaddressed by design — see my previous comment on this task; it needs a CTO ruling, not an implementer's default.

IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE (developer-marcus) — branch feat/AS-93-deep-link-host, 3 commits (ca3b4a1 helper + unit tests + STATIC_FILES; a22c638 three call sites + /api/config + lib/lattice.js warning comment + api tests; f0de2ec README), 373 changed lines, split trigger never fired. Suite with --build receipts (Image asc-as93-marcus-test Built): baseline 20 files / 286 tests / 286 pass; final 21 / 293 / 293 (+7, exactly the projection). Mutations 8/8 observed red on detached scratch worktrees with asserted grep transitions; three predictions in plan section 5 were wrong (M-BASELINE and M-AC1 wider by T4/T2 because T4 is inference-coupled by construction and T2 spans all four loopback spellings; M-AC5 leaves T6 green because T6 asserts the server endpoint and only T4 can observe the override at a rendered href — AC-5 client half rests on T4 alone). Deviation: dashHref is a function declaration so the plan T7 count (3 sites + 1 definition) stays honest. OPEN FOR THE CTO before merge: the board commented on this task from the dashboard (15:30Z) that the lattice port is not fixed; the plan hard-codes 8799 and 8443, and 8443 is only right because Tailscale maps it to 8799 — Marcus filed the options in his comment and recommends leaving 8799 with AS-94 (the launchd job) owning the port. The review tick should get Owen's ruling on that and pass it to QA as context, not as a verdict.
